text.p: Sporting coach Robert Waseige resigned on Sunday after another indifferent performance from the Lisbon side provoked protests from supporters.
The Belgian coach, who took over at Sporting at the start of the season, offered his resignation after his side could only manage a 0-0 home draw with Uniao de Leiria.
Sporting said that the resignation had been accepted and that former deputy trainer Octavio Machado would take over the running of the club.
Waseige had been under pressure for sometime after a string of disappointing results.

On Sunday, supporters jeered the team for the second home game in succession. Sporting, who have not won the Portuguese championship for 14 years, lie in third place in the league but a distant nine points behind leaders Porto.
Defending champions Porto, who beat Leca 4-2 away on Friday, stay top of the first division with 32 points, followed by Benfica with 29 and Sporting on 23. Benfica beat Rio Ave 1-0 on Saturday.

A goal by Leca striker Constantino Jardim in the second minute did not intimidate Porto, who went 2-1 ahead by halftime with goals by Brazilians Mario Jardel in the ninth minute and Edmilson Pimenta in the 24th.
Edmilson scored his second goal in the 57th minute and Rui Barros made it 4-1 in the 70th minute. Jose da Rocha reduced the deficit from a pass by Jardim in the 73rd minute.
